newsitem.title: USA: Bullion Monarch sets Knomex control.
newsitem.headline: Bullion Monarch sets Knomex control.

text.p: Bullion Monarch Co said it tentatively agreed to become the controlling shareholder of Knomex Redsources Inc.

Bullion Monarch said it entered into a Letter of Intent whereby Knomex will acquire from Bullion Monarch the Austin Mill, an interest in the Austin Dumps, two silver properties and a 5 percent net smelter returns royalty in the Adelaide Property in consideration for the issuance of 20 million units of Knomex priced at $0.20 per unit with each unit being comprised of one common share and one warrant to purchase a further common share at $0.20 for two years following closing.

In addition, Bullion Monarch said, it signed letter of intent with three shareholders of Knomex to acquire privately an aggregate of 9 million Knomex common shares, including 3 million to be acquired from St. Columban Resources Inc, a private Canadian company, in exchange for common shares of Bullion Monarch if the Austin Mill transaction closes.

If the Austin Mill transaction is approved by shareholders and regulatory authorities and Bullion Monarch acquires 9 million Knomex shares privately, it will become the controlling shareholder of Knomex.

In a related transaction, St. Columban has agreed to make a private placement of US $2.5 million into Bullion Monarch in exchange for 5 million units of Bullion Monarch priced at $0.50 per unit with each unit being comprised of one common share and one warrant to purchase a further common share at $0.50 for two years following the closing of the transaction.
This private placement is conditional upon the closing of the Austin Mill transaction, Bullion Monarch said.
St. Columban has reached a verbal agreement with certain shareholders of Bullion Monarch to acquire from them 1.5 million Bullion Monarch common shares in exchange for common shares of St. Columban.
As a result of these transactions, St. Columban will become a controlling shareholder of Bullion Monarch, the company said.

Bullion Monarch also said it tentgatively agreed to acquire from Gold Valley Resources Inc a package of properties with a value of US $1 million in exchange for 2 million units with the same terms as the warrants being sold to St. Columban plus a second warrant to purchase a further common share at US $0.75 for two years following the closing of the transaction. ((-- New York Newsdesk 212-859-1610.))
